topic.title: What Inflation Really Does to Your Savings
topic.hook: Sitting still is a decision with a cost
topic.payoff: Sitting still is a decision with a cost

copy.kicker: The machine runs whether you watch it or not.
copy.thumb_scene: Wick stands upright on a plain white studio background, arms loose at his sides, holding a clear glass jar of coins in one hand while a thick stack of paper currency fans out visibly thinner at the top, the two objects placed side by side in front of him as he stares directly into the camera with a flat, unblinking expression.
copy.send_to: the friend whose savings account hasn't moved in two years

caption:
Most people think doing nothing is neutral.

It compounds.

Inaction is not a pause. It is a direction.

The hidden rule is this: the longer your behaviour goes unobserved, the more your systems run on defaults someone else designed, and those defaults are never built in your favour.

Six untracked months is money leaving through doors you forgot you opened. Two years is an identity the algorithm assembled for you. Five years is a gap between where you are and where you meant to be that now has a number attached to it.

Wake up.

What is one thing you stopped watching that you now suspect has been running without you?

Light one. Pass it on. 🕯️
